Hi Alex / Priya —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Below is a concise recap of what we captured on the call and the proposed next steps so we have alignment. Please flag anything I missed.

1) Business context & success criteria- Primary goal: run patient-identifiable inference workflows for clinical decision support in the US while meeting strict data sovereignty and audit requirements.- Success criteria: zero exfiltration of PHI, KMS integration with customer-managed keys, demonstrable audit logs for model inputs/outputs, and SLA for inference latency < 500ms p95 on average production queries.- Timeline: pilot environment within 6–8 weeks; production readiness for one center within 12–16 weeks (subject to legal/procurement).

2) Key constraints and risk items discussed- Data residency: data must remain within ClearPath-owned VPCs in AWS us-east-1; no routing through third-party control planes.- Air-gap requirement: one or more sites may require an air-gapped deployment (no internet egress), especially for clinical trial workloads.- KMS: customer must bring KMS (AWS KMS / HSM) keys; Redwood must support decrypt-only operations and never persist plaintext keys.- Network: limited outbound ports, strict whitelisting; egress to Redwood control plane not allowed for air-gapped customers.- Compliance artifacts requested: SOC 2 report, summary of logging retention/process, and attestations around KV cache handling.

3) Current stack (what you shared)- Primary infra: ClearPath uses AWS accounts per center (us-east-1) with transit gateway for inter-center connectivity.- CI/CD: fully internal for regulated workloads; uses signed artifacts only.- Security: Splunk for SIEM, Palo Alto NGFW, and dedicated KMS per account.

4) Proposed Redwood approaches (short)- Option A (VPC-only, customer-managed control plane): Redwood deploys inference runtime into your AWS accounts (customer-managed), integrates with your KMS, and uses peered networking. Minimal internet egress; our control-plane access can be restricted to management VPCs.- Option B (Air-gapped on-prem image): a fully isolated package (air-gapped) that runs without external egress; updates via signed bundles delivered over secure channel. Suitable for trial sites that require total isolation.- Note: both options include our telemetry-free mode for PHI and configurable audit logging to feed Splunk.

5) Immediate next steps (owner / ETA)- Action (Redwood): share deployment checklist + network template and an air-gap option brief — Sofia — EOD Friday (2027-06-04). Attachment: redwood_deploy_checklist_v1.pdf- Action (ClearPath): confirm whether the pilot site requires air-gap or VPC-only, and share a sanitized network diagram and a list of blocked outbound ports — Alex/Priya — by EOW (2027-06-10). Attachment template: clearpath_network_constraints.xlsx- Action (Redwood engineering): schedule technical deep-dive with Dev and Marcus to validate KMS integration approach — Sofia to propose times — by 2027-06-07.

Attachments: redwood_deploy_checklist_v1.pdf (checklist), clearpath_network_constraints.xlsx (sample template).

Thanks — I’ll upload the checklist and a short one-pager on our air-gap option to the Drive folder and send calendar invites for the technical deep-dive.

Quick notes ahead of the deep-dive: 

- KMS: cross-account AWS KMS with grant-only IAM roles looks clean for the pilot; no plaintext keys in Redwood runtime. For air-gapped HSMs, we can support a signing-only agent that validates signed model bundles and performs decryption within a customer-controlled enclave.
- Network: for non-airgapped pilot, we should request a small outbound allowlist: 443 to our management IPs for orchestration + S3 signed URL access for model artifacts. For air-gapped, we rely on signed bundles pushed via a secure USB or a private data diode transfer; we should document patch/update cadence and rollback path.
- Observability: we propose a telemetry-free mode where only non-PII metrics (latency, token counts) are exported. For audit logs, we can emit hashed input IDs and encrypted audit artifacts into S3 in the customer account with lifecycle rules.

I attached a short comparison doc for air-gap vs VPC-only decisions (airgap_option_comparison.pdf). Happy to walk through during the call.
